items.title: Daily Water Minute · The $2,920 math nobody talks about
items.preview:
Words I like;
"If you can't measure it, you can't improve it." Peter Drucker said that about business, but it works for your wallet too.
Here's the math most people never do: one 24-pack of bottled water runs about $6 these days. If your family goes through two packs a week (pretty normal for a household of four), that's $624 a year. Over five years? $3,120. Over ten? $6,240.
And that's conservative. Add in the gas stations, the vending machines, the convenience store runs when you're out, and the real number climbs fast.
Nobody wakes up and says "I want to spend three grand on plastic bottles." It just happens a case at a time.
For folks who already have a ClearWave system, you know this. You did the math before you called us. You're drinking straight from the tap now, and that $50-a-month habit is gone.
For everyone else: I'm not saying bottled water is evil. I'm saying it's expensive, and most people genuinely don't realize how expensive until they add it up.
There's a better way. It starts with knowing what's actually in your water.
Hit reply and I'll send you our free water assessment.
As promised, value in under a minute.
Justin
CEO / ClearWave

items.title: Email Campaign · 1: 1-Year Annual Service Reminder

### Email Body

Don,
Your Ironmax + Acid Neutralizer hit the one-year mark last week.

Book online here: [SCHEDULING_LINK]

Justin
CEO / ClearWave

**P.S.** If a neighbor asks about your water, send them our way. You'll get $500 cash when they close, and they'll get a free water assessment to start. More here: [REFERRAL_PAGE_LINK]
---
### Send Timing
**Tuesday, 10:00 AM ET**
Rationale: Mid-morning Tuesday historically performs best for transactional service emails (avoid Monday chaos, beat Wednesday-Thursday inbox fatigue).
### Expected Performance
- **Open rate:** 52% (service reminder + personalized first name in subject line; higher urgency than educational content)
- **Click rate:** 8% (single clear CTA, time-sensitive maintenance action)
- **Conversion (booked appts):** 35% = ~9 bookings (industry avg for annual service reminders is 25; 40%; ClearWave's high trust + locked-in pricing drives upper end)
### Notes
- Personalized first line with client name + actual system ("Your Ironmax + Acid Neutralizer")
- Hard rule compliance: says "your Ironmax + Acid Neutralizer," not "your ClearWave"
- Includes soft referral plug in P.S. (natural, not pushy; uses exact $500 / "free water assessment" language)
- No em dashes anywhere
- Sign-off is exact two-line format

items.title: Email Campaign · 2: Cold Lead Re-Engagement (New Water News Hook)
items.preview:
**Audience:** 1,000 cold subscribers (>60d no engagement, never reached quote stage)
**Source:** IDEA_SOURCING.md § Re-engagement campaigns > "Did something change?" + Educational content repurposing > water news angle
### Subject Lines
**Primary:**
`VA's new PFAS limits (what it means for you)`
**Alternates:**
1. `The EPA just moved the goalposts`
2. `Forever chemicals: new rules, real answers`
3. `Your water question from 6 months ago`
4. `We haven't talked in a while. Here's why.`
### Preview Text
`New federal limits on PFAS went live this month. If you're on city water, here's what changed.`
### Email Body
Subject: VA's new PFAS limits (what it means for you)
You signed up for ClearWave emails a while back.
We haven't been in touch recently, so I wanted to restart with something actually useful.
**What just changed:**
The EPA finalized new federal limits on PFAS (per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances, also called "forever chemicals") in public drinking water. The rules took effect April 2026.
If you're on city water in Virginia, your utility now has to test for six specific PFAS compounds and take action if levels exceed the new thresholds.
**What that means for your home:**
City water that passes federal limits is legally safe. But "legally safe" and "what I want my kids drinking" are sometimes two different conversations.
Most city water systems in our area will comply. A few may not. Either way, you won't know your home's specific level unless you test at the tap (city testing happens at the treatment plant, not your faucet).
**If you want to know where you stand:**
We offer a free water assessment. Takes 20 minutes. We test at your kitchen sink, explain what's in your water (including PFAS risk factors), and show you what it would take to remove it if you decide you want to.
No pressure. No sales pitch if you're happy with what you've got.
Book here: [SCHEDULING_LINK]
Or just reply to this email with your address and preferred day/time.
Justin
CEO / ClearWave
---
**P.S.** If your water's fine and you just want to stay in the loop on this stuff, you're welcome to stay subscribed. I'll only email when there's something worth reading.
---
### Send Timing
**Thursday, 9:00 AM ET**
Rationale: Thursday morning for educational content allows weekend consideration window.避oids service-email Tuesday slot. Cold leads need softer, "here's value first" timing.
### Expected Performance
- **Open rate:** 26% (cold segment, but timely/newsy subject line lifts above avg; educational hook resets relationship)
- **Click rate:** 2.5% (realistic for re-engagement; we're asking for a meeting, not a micro-commitment)
- **Conversion (booked assessments):** 1.2% = ~12 bookings (cold leads convert at 1; 2%; new news hook + clear CTA + low-pressure tone optimizes within that range)
- **List hygiene bonus:** expect 3; 5% unsubscribe rate, which is healthy (removes true dead weight, improves deliverability)
### Notes
- Does NOT say "still interested?" or "we miss you" (stale)
- Leads with NEW external value (EPA PFAS rule is real, recent, and relevant)
- Uses "free water assessment" exactly (hard rule #3a)
- Acknowledges the gap ("we haven't been in touch") without apologizing
- Gives permission to stay subscribed without action (reduces unsubscribe spite)
- Tone is educational + helpful, not salesy (luxury_product register)
- No em dashes
- Sign-off is exact two-line format
---
## Why These 2?
1. **Annual service (26 people):** Highest conversion rate, shortest sales cycle, guaranteed revenue ($349 × 9 expected bookings = $3,141), and keeps systems healthy (retention play). This is low-hanging fruit with a 12-month trigger that only fires once per customer.
2. **Cold lead re-engagement (1,000 people):** Largest addressable audience with zero recent contact. New PFAS news gives us a legitimate reason to re-enter the inbox without looking desperate. Even at 1.2% conversion, that's 12 net-new assessment bookings from people who've gone dark. High upside, low downside (unsubscribes clean the list).
**Not chosen this week:**
- **Referral push (17 people):** Small audience, and referral asks work better as P.S. plugs in service emails (captured in Campaign 1) than as standalone campaigns.
- **RO replacement (25 people):** Solid audience, but RO filter swaps are often DIY or handled ad hoc; lower urgency than annual service.
- **Concierge upsell (100 people):** Larger audience, but needs a multi-touch sequence (not a one-off blast). Better as a May drip campaign after annual service reminders clear.

---
